summary: Iteration 2 testing: 14/15 backend pytest passed (93%). Frontend flows verified: forgot-password dialog, reset-password page, Dashboard overdue-banner + /weekly nav, ObjectiveDetail Updates tab rendering 2 recharts SVGs, ObjectiveDetail AI-analysis tab with Run button. One CRITICAL backend bug: brute-force lockout is effectively broken in the deployed environment because it identifies clients by request.client.host which rotates across Kubernetes ingress proxy pod IPs (e.g. 10.64.130.9, 10.64.129.166). AI endpoints (Gemini 3 Flash) work end-to-end: evaluate-objective and evaluate-individual return correct schema-validated JSON; role gating correct; evaluations persist and listable.

critical.issue: Lockout uses identifier=`{request.client.host}:{email}`. In the k8s ingress deployment, request.client.host is the connecting proxy pod IP, which rotates across multiple ingress replicas. 6 consecutive failed attempts from the same external client produced login_attempts docs with count=4 and count=2 on two different proxy IPs -- neither reaches MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS=5, so 429 is never returned. Effectively disables the security feature in production. Fix: use request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for').split(',')[0].strip() as the IP (fallback to request.client.host).

issues: DialogContent missing Description/aria-describedby (a11y warning, not blocking)

action_items: FIX HIGH: /api/auth/login brute-force lockout -- replace request.client.host with x-forwarded-for (first IP) so counter accumulates per real client. Verify by running 5 failed logins from same external IP and expecting 6th to return 429.
Optional: Add aria-describedby/DialogDescription to the forgot-password DialogContent to silence a11y warnings.

Brute-force lockout logic itself is correct in isolation; the IP-detection is the only defect.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout ineffective in production. REPRODUCTION: from a single external client, POST /api/auth/login with a valid email and wrong password 6 times. Expected: 6th returns 429. Actual: all 6 return 401. Inspecting db.login_attempts shows TWO (or more) docs with identifiers like `10.64.130.9:email` (count=4) and `10.64.129.166:email` (count=2), summing to 6 but neither reaching 5. CAUSE: `request.client.host` in FastAPI reports the immediate TCP peer, which is the Kubernetes ingress-nginx controller pod -- there are multiple replicas load-balancing traffic. MITIGATION: replace the ip extraction with `ip = (request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') or '').split(',')[0].strip() or (request.client.host if request.client else 'unknown')`. Also consider rate-limiting purely by email to prevent distributed/headless attacks.
